title: An Empirical Investigation of Learning from Biased Toxicity Labels
findings: The paper does not provide findings specific to religion, but aggregates results across 13 identity groups, which includes a 'religion' category. The main finding is that there is a trade-off between model accuracy and fairness, with no single training strategy performing best on all metrics. Models fine-tuned on a small amount of clean data (after initial training on large, noisy data) achieved the highest overall accuracy and performed best on accuracy-based fairness metrics. However, a model trained only on the small, clean dataset showed the least bias on the accuracy-agnostic Negative Average Equality Gap metric.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures fairness metrics (Subgroup AUC, Background Positive Subgroup Negative AUC, and Negative Average Equality Gap) for a toxicity classification task. This evaluation specifically assesses unintended bias against 13 different identity groups, which include religion as one of the categories.
